name: Flint (nodular chalcedony from the chalk), freshly broken

diffuseAlbedo.source: Munsell N3 (blue-black), the broken face of chalk flint as field descriptions give it; its white cortex is not the broken face
diffuseAlbedo.note: No measured colour of the site's own ground was read: a first colour from the Munsell notation field descriptions give the layer, converted approximately.

refractiveIndex.source: Handbook of Mineralogy, Quartz (Anthony, Bideaux, Bladh and Nichols, Mineralogical Society of America): n omega 1.544 (chalcedony is microcrystalline quartz)

porosity.source: Flint is a near-solid chalcedony: a first value of a few per cent micro-porosity

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.source: Docs/Stages/cube.md section 7 (the ground rule's relief and stones)
grain.note: The finest structure the face shows.

bed.source: Docs/Stages/cube.md section 7 (the ground rule's relief and stones)
bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the topsoil's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
